A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hawkes-process causal discovery framework. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support comparison; visual inspection resolved extraction difficulties.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic experiments, sensitivity analyses, and causal-graph recovery on cellular-network data in Section 5 and Appendix Q.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, threshold sensitivity, runtime measurements, and merged-device analysis in Section 6 and Appendix Q.

M1.justification: V2 Algorithm 1 removes v1's initial step excluding subprocesses that are unconditionally locally independent of others. This changes the stated preprocessing procedure, while the alternating discovery phases, surrogate construction, and rank tests remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: The six synthetic graph families, directly generated discrete-time data, and larger 14-subprocess graph are retained. V2 adds evaluation on all 18 alarm types after merging all 55 devices, extending coverage to a broader, heterogeneous input setting within the existing cellular dataset.

E2.justification: V2 adds LPCMCI to the five retained synthetic baselines in Figures 4 and 8. It also introduces quantitative comparisons against SHP, THP, NPHC, Hier. Rank, RLCD, and LPCMCI on the cellular sub-dataset in Table 6, where v1 reported only its own inferred graph. This substantially expands comparator participation.

E3.justification: New protocols include a four-threshold sweep on 30k samples, runtime measurement, and grid-searched real-data comparisons. Figure 10 also revises the reference graph by adding Alarm_id=3 → Alarm_id=2. Existing synthetic settings and F1 matching rules remain; the newly specified device_id=8 does not establish that the earlier device selection changed.

E4.justification: Appendix Q adds analyses of rank-test threshold sensitivity, runtime across different graph structures, and recovery after merging heterogeneous devices. These substantially extend practical sensitivity, scalability, and failure-case evidence. The earlier discretization, rank-faithfulness, and larger-graph analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten-run averages without uncertainty intervals. V2 removes checklist item 7, which explicitly described independent trials, synthetic-data generation as the principal source of variability, and the rationale for omitting error bars. The additional tables otherwise follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds threshold and runtime results, cellular comparisons (Table 6: ours 0.76 versus SHP 0.49), and merged-device F1 of 0.17. Added LPCMCI results include approximately 0.67 versus Ours (Hawkes) 0.63 at 30k samples in Case 2. The inferred cellular graph gains Alarm_id=3 → Alarm_id=2. Earlier synthetic curves and Tables 1–3, now Tables 1, 3, and 4, retain their values; no overall same-setting performance gain is established.

T1.justification: V2 removes the non-isolation or local-dependence exclusions from v1 Propositions 3.3 and 3.5 and Theorem 3.8, now numbered 4.3, 4.5, and 4.8, broadening their stated domains. Appendix N adds an argument asserting sound abstention when the path condition fails. The main mathematical framework and most proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims of latent-subprocess discovery, rank-based identification, and a two-phase algorithm remain. V2 omits v1's explicit concluding claim that the approach naturally extends to discrete time-series data, modestly narrowing its advertised applicability while retaining the discrete-time experiments.

C2.justification: V2 attributes poor merged-device recovery to heterogeneous generative mechanisms and explains why per-device analysis better matches its assumptions. It also interprets threshold precision–recall tradeoffs and runtime differences through latent attenuation and algorithm iterations. These are targeted additions to the retained interpretations and limitations.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents device_id=8, rank-threshold grid search and the recommended value 0.10, a correlation-based suggestion for selecting effective lags, and the AMD EPYC 9454 CPU used for runtime profiling. It removes v1's statement that demonstration code accompanies the supplement; the PDFs do not establish actual code withdrawal.

R1.justification: V2 adds a main-text Related Work section and substantially expands Appendix A with detailed positioning against binned-Hawkes estimation and rank-based latent discovery. It explicitly contrasts temporal ordering, structural assumptions, and cardinality requirements, adds LPCMCI's citation, and removes several earlier references, including Koyama's coarse-grained Hawkes work.

P1.justification: The introduction, methodological explanations, related work, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. V2 inserts Section 2, subdivides the rank-discovery exposition, and replaces the NeurIPS checklist with shorter ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-usage statements. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond scientific additions.

P2.justification: V2 adds three tables, expands Figure 1 with a latent-confounder panel, adds LPCMCI curves and legends to Figures 4 and 8, and redraws the cellular graphs with revised labels and an additional edge. Denser typography and relocation of appendix algorithms also substantially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 supplements v1's qualitative cellular example with quantitative comparisons, threshold sensitivity, measured computational costs, and a disclosed merged-device failure case. Clearer positioning and implementation details make applicability easier to assess. These gains remain bounded by the small principal real-data example and absent uncertainty estimates. Some useful checklist disclosures disappear, and broadened theorem hypotheses receive little additional proof support.
